predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Egypt, to which Muhammad ibn Tughj was appointed governor in 935 and which he entered at Fustat on 26 August 935

successors.name: Fatimid Caliphate
successors.text: Egypt (Fustat taken 6 July 969), Palestine (May 970) and Damascus (November 970)

rulers.name: Abu al-Fawaris Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Ikhshid

ledger.x: 935: Muhammad ibn Tughj enters Fustat and founds Ikhshidid Egypt.
936: the Ikhshidids occupy Syria up to Aleppo.
939: Muhammad ibn Ra'iq claims Syria.
939: the north of Syria passes to Ibn Ra'iq, the Abbasid commander (amir al-umara).
940: after fighting at al-Arish and Lajjun, 'a treaty restores the previous borders, with al-Ikhshid paying 140,000 gold dinars in annual tribute'.
942: Ibn Ra'iq is assassinated (April) and in June 'al-Ikhshid reoccupies Syria and reaches Damascus', returning to Egypt in January 943.
944: the caliph grants Ibn Tughj's family the Hejaz.
944: Sayf al-Dawla takes Aleppo.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 944: the Ikhshidids and Hamdanids fight over northern Syria and Damascus.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 945: the treaty of October divides Syria.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 946: Damascus drawn as Hamdanid for the year as bridging.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 946: war resumes at Damascus.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 947: Kafur recovers Damascus.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 947: the fight for Damascus ends with the Ikhshidid settlement; Sayf al-Dawla keeps northern Syria and 'recognized Kafur's lordship over parts of Syria' (no year given).
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 969: Mecca turns to the Fatimids.
969: the Fatimid army enters the Delta.
969: Fustat falls to the Fatimids.
969: the fight for Egypt ends with the Fatimid possession of Fustat (6 July 969); the remnant of the dynasty holds only southern Syria and Palestine.
970: the Ikhshidid regent in Palestine is beaten.
970: Damascus falls.
970: the last Ikhshidid holdings fall to the Fatimids.

wars.name: Fatimid attack on Egypt (935-936)
wars.outcome: The Fatimids captured Alexandria in March 936 and al-Hasan ibn Tughj retook it on 31 March; the Ikhshidid page says Ubayd Allah defeated the Fatimids by November 936.

wars.name: Ikhshidid war with Muhammad ibn Ra'iq
wars.outcome: Syria was partitioned in 939 (Ramla and the south to al-Ikhshid), the 940 treaty restored the borders against 140,000 dinars of tribute, and Ibn Ra'iq's assassination in April 942 let al-Ikhshid reoccupy Syria in June.

wars.name: Ikhshidid-Hamdanid war over Syria
wars.outcome: Sayf al-Dawla took Aleppo and northern Syria (October 944); al-Ikhshid beat him near Qinnasrin in 945 and the October 945 treaty gave the north to the Hamdanids and Damascus and the south to the Ikhshidids; fighting at Damascus resumed in 946 and Kafur…

wars.name: Fatimid conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Jawhar took Alexandria (May 969) and Fustat (6 July 969); the Ikhshidid leader al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah was captured in May 970 and Damascus surrendered in November 970.
